extracted.intended_audience: graduate students, researchers, and scholars in philosophy of science, history/sociology of science, and related fields interested in evolutionary models of scientific change
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and diagnostic features for evaluating whether scientific practices and communities exhibit the signature properties of Darwinian (selection-driven) adaptive processes — e.g., stability/isolation, epistemic selection pressures, convergence/multiples, and the characteristic dynamics of adaptive walks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and isolation of the population
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific practices must exhibit sufficient stability and isolation for directional evolution to operate (the chapter: “general importance of stability and isolation for facilitating directional evolution, and of the particular talent of niche constructors for promoting stability and isolation”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability/isolation make selective retention effective; niche construction by practitioners promotes the conditions under which selection can push a community toward particular practice-clusters. Without stability and isolation, adaptive refinement toward an optimum is impeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and strength of epistemic selection pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Epistemic selection pressures are selection pressures that take the form of practitioners’ preferences for certain kinds of practices over others (explicit phrase: “epistemic selection pressures (i.e., selection pressures that take the form of practitioners’ preferences for certain kinds of practices over others)”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether community norms, incentives, and evaluative procedures preferentially retain practices that improve knowledge; strong epistemic preferences are required for selection-like optimization of practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of internal selection mechanisms (e.g., proposal review) as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes internal to science—such as the research proposal review process—are empirically informative about the magnitudes of selective pressures (text: “the quantitative data on research proposal review from the NIH sends a very strong signal in direct support of the generalized dominance of epistemic pressures”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional mechanisms (peer review, grant decisions) as observable proxies for selection pressures. If expert reviewers consistently privilege proposals that increase knowledge, this supports the claim that epistemic selection pressures are operative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solving record of the community
rubrics_metrics.description: Communities routinely formulate problems and develop theories that eventually solve those problems; rapid and routine problem solving suggests that solving those problems matters for reproductive success of practices (section: “the problems that these communities set for themselves do tend to get solved”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the community’s chosen problems are in fact being solved with some regularity; a strong track record of problem solving is evidence that selection favors problem-solving practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment between prestige incentives and epistemic goals
rubrics_metrics.description: If prestige (or other social commodities) drives behavior, then to support epistemic selection the means of achieving prestige must be tied to problem solving or epistemic improvement (discussion of the prestige objection and response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between prestige as an independent driver and prestige that is correlated with epistemic success. If prestige is achieved primarily via problem solving, invoking prestige does not undermine epistemic explanations; evaluate whether prestige-seeking behavior tends to reward epistemically valuable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-fidelity copying is insufficient; need directional pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: High-fidelity copying alone cannot account for sustained clustering (clumpiness) of practice space—directional pressures (selection) are required to explain continued clustering beyond initial conditions (text: “High-fidelity copying alone cannot account for sustained clumpiness, only for initially clumpy conditions”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish mere retention/copying from selective retention that alters relative frequencies; look for mechanisms that preferentially increase the prevalence of certain practices rather than merely preserving initial distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clumpiness and constraints on movement in practice space
rubrics_metrics.description: The empirical observation that occupied points in practice space are densely clustered suggests strong constraints on practitioners’ ability to adopt sufficiently different practices (phrases: “movement within it is severely restricted—that is, that there are strong constraints on a practitioner’s ability to adopt practices that are sufficiently different from the ones with which he began”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree to which practice-space occupancy is clustered and whether practitioners’ transitions to distant practice-clusters are rare; strong constraints on mobility support directional convergence explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevalence of convergence and multiple independent discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent independent multiple discovery (Merton’s ‘in principle multiples’) is evidence of directional tendencies in inquiry (text: “scientific discoveries were ‘in principle multiples’ … scientific inquiry, by its very nature, drives independent practitioners to the same point in practice space”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the rate and frequency of independent rediscovery or near-simultaneous discovery as a diagnostic for directionality: high prevalence suggests that the practice-space dynamics channel practitioners toward the same solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of rate of scientific communication on simultaneity
rubrics_metrics.description: As scientific communication speed increases, multiples get closer together in time and can become virtually simultaneous; faster diffusion makes community-level constraints act more synchronously (text discussing Simonton’s findings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider communication/diffusion speed as a moderator: rapid communication increases simultaneity of arrivals at practice-points, strengthening the appearance of multiple independent discoveries driven by shared constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive landscape criteria for local optima
rubrics_metrics.description: An adaptive scenario’s limit is a state where (1) the population’s phenotypic mean is at a local optimum, (2) there is no accessible phenotypic state that improves adaptedness, and (3) even slight deviations from this optimal phenotype are penalized by selection (text: canonical Modern Synthetic picture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnose whether the community has reached practice-cluster optima by checking that small deviations reduce epistemic fitness and no accessible alternative practice yields improvement; these are the hallmark conditions of an adaptive peak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive-walk signature: initial large gains and declining step sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptive walks typically show that the inaugural step accounts for a large portion of total gain; the largest single-step increase is on average at least ~50% of overall gain; and contributions decline approximately geometrically so step sizes shrink over the course of the walk (summarizing Orr and Gillespie results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for historical sequences in which early innovations produce large epistemic gains followed by progressively smaller refinements — a pattern consistent with Darwinian adaptive walks rather than other forms of directional change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity / accessibility of intermediate variants
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevance of Godfrey-Smith’s ‘Continuity’ condition: adaptive refinement requires that favorable changes can be achieved via sequences of intermediate, accessible modifications (text: significance of Godfrey-Smith’s “Continuity” condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether transitions between practices can occur by small, accessible steps (continuity), since large leaps that lack intermediate states undermine the standard Darwinian adaptive-walk model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to distinguish selection-driven convergence from other directional forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergence in practice space does not by itself imply natural selection; many systems converge for other directional reasons, so one must test for signature properties of evolutionary adaptation before attributing convergence to selection (text: “Even if convergence is symptomatic of a system under the influence of directional pressure, however, that does not thereby mean that the source of the directional pressure is natural selection”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply diagnostic tests (e.g., adaptive-walk signatures, selection-like retention mechanisms, penalization of deviations) rather than inferring evolutionary adaptation from convergence alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing of profitable options approaching an optimum
rubrics_metrics.description: As a community approaches an optimal state, the sphere of favorable variation shrinks and options for profitable improvement narrow so that a single move can become uniquely salient (text: “options for improvement tend to narrow as one approaches any optimum” and discussion of chess-analogy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect progressive constraint: the more knowledge/community convergence there is, the fewer distinct profitable investigations remain; this narrowing predicts increased simultaneity of similar moves by different practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain variability in susceptibility to adaptive refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all domains are equally susceptible to independence-of-multiples or selection-driven convergence (text: e.g., pure mathematics and theoretical physics may be less susceptible than microbiology; role of uniquely human ingenuity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor in domain-specific differences — evaluate whether a domain’s reliance on unique problem-solving creativity versus routine incremental ‘mop-up’ work makes it more or less likely to exhibit Darwinian adaptive refinement.
